natural_language: Two strictly positive parameters are given, named first and second. A real-valued random variable Z is normally distributed. Its scale is second and its location is first — the same assignment as the reference form, written with the two roles in the opposite textual order. Decide whether this is the same object as the reference.

expected_semantics.relation_to_reference: same meaning; must share a canonical hash
expected_semantics.note: argument ORDER is not part of identity because roles are labelled

distractors: Judging this different from the reference because the text differs. Under labelled roles the textual order is not meaning-bearing.

Generalising from this case that the canonical hash detects semantic equivalence. It detects a narrow syntactic normalisation: argument order and bound-variable spelling. It does NOT identify 'a > 0' with '0 < a', nor reordered statements.
